text:
alex: Heads-up — we saw a ~28% tail-latency regression on the 16xA100 PP(4)/TP(4) stack after landing the activation-checkpointing change set. Bulk of the increase looks network-related, but there's a weird KV-cache interaction too. attaching short profiler excerpt below.

alex: Profile summary (from /tmp/run_2026-03-17.prof):
```
compute_forward: 22.1%
recompute_forward: 18.9%
all_reduce / inter-node: 39.7%  <-- huge jump
kv_cache_update: 6.6% (spikes at seq start)
other_sync: 4.5%
overlap_efficiency: -7.8%  # negative means comms blocking compute
```

alex: Context: we enabled chunked activation checkpointing (checkpoint_interval=2) + aggressive continuous batching (batch_window_ms=25) and a recent kernel-selection change that picks the "fused_gemm_attn_v2" path for medium length sequences.

maria: Interesting. My guess: checkpointing increased recompute windows so TP stages are producing bursts of gradients that trigger immediate all-reduces, which defeats our batching/fusion window. Also fused kernel may change timing so KV cache writes/reads collide with collectives.

david: Agreed. Two concrete suspects: 1) NCCL fusion threshold or op fusion is too low now (so we get many small all-reduces), 2) KV cache writeback happens synchronously during the same CUDA stream as the all-reduce.

kevin: Quick check: can you paste the NCCL envs used for the run? especially NCCL_ALGO, NCCL_BUF_SIZE, NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS, PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF.

alex: Here you go: 
```
NCCL_ALGO=ring
NCCL_BUFFSIZE=2097152
NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=2
NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=0
PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.7,max_split_size_mb:64
```

perf-bot: I found the previous run (two weeks ago) with no checkpointing: all_reduce was ~18% and overlap_efficiency +3.1%. Logs: https://perf.redwood/triage/1843.

maria: So checkpointing doubled all-reduce time. Two-prong plan: (A) try raising NCCL_BUFFSIZE and enabling fusion window tuning; (B) change checkpointing to selective (skip attention checkpointing) to test if KV-cache writes are the trigger.

david: Also test switching the kernel-selection override to prefer the non-fused path for this workload (kernel_selector=legacy_attn_first) — if the fused kernel shifts compute earlier it may reduce overlap opportunity.

kevin: I can run a small matrix. Proposed experiments: 
- baseline: no checkpointing, fused kernel (existing good run)
- A1: checkpointing (interval=2), fused kernel, NCCL_BUFFSIZE=8MB
- A2: checkpointing (interval=2), fused kernel, NCCL_BUFFSIZE=32MB + NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=4
- B1: checkpointing selective (skip attention), fused kernel
- C1: checkpointing (interval=2), kernel_selector=legacy_attn_first

alex: Great. For the selective checkpointing config, use this snippet: 
```
"checkpointing": {
  "enabled": true,
  "interval": 2,
  "skip_modules": ["attention", "layernorm"]
}
```

maria: Small optimization idea: move KV cache updates to a dedicated stream and mark them as non-blocking with cudaEvent-based ordering. That should decouple cache IO from collectives. Can we prototype that without a full runtime release? Maybe a runtime flag kv_async_stream=true.

david: I prototyped kv_async_stream in a branch — it's low-risk: it posts cache writes to stream 2 and only blocks the consuming ops with an event. I can push a tryjob if we want to validate.

kevin: Please do — run A2 + C1 + kv_async_stream=true as a combined test. If kv_async_stream cuts all_reduce by ~10-15% and overlap_efficiency goes positive, we likely have a real ordering contention.

alex: Assigning: kevin -> run the experiment matrix, david -> push kv_async_stream tryjob and a kernel_selector toggle build, maria -> instrument KV cache histograms at per-step granularity, I'll do end-to-end traces and aggregate the perf counters.

alex: Timeline: can we get the first batch of runs within 24h? If we see regressions, we may hotfix to selective checkpointing for customers on 16-GPU configs.

perf-bot: Scheduled tryjobs: job/1843001 (A2 + kv_async_stream) queued; job/1843002 (C1) queued. ETA ~6h.

maria: A couple of notes for the report: capture per-stage send/recv sizes (NCCL op sizes), counts of all-reduce calls per step, and KV cache event timestamps. Those will show if collectives fragmentation is the root cause.

kevin: Will attach the run matrix and a small Jupyter that compares p99 and all_reduce time across runs.

alex: Thanks all. If anyone has an urgent idea — drop it here; otherwise we'll reconvene after tryjob results. :thumbsup:
